songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Epic Dark Star marathon with tight St. Stephen → Mason's flow
ai_show_review.blurb: The set is anchored by a marathon Dark Star that showcases Garcia’s smoking solo and tight interplay with Phil. A seamless Saint Stephen → Mason’s Children transition keeps the momentum high, while Good Lovin’, Uncle John’s Band and a double Turn On Your Lovelight round out a powerful performance.
ai_show_review.review: On February 2, 1970 at St. Louis’ Fox Theatre the Dead delivered one of their most memorable early‑70 shows. The night is defined by an almost twenty‑minute Dark Star that has been described as “epic,” “transcendent,” and “smoking” – a true showcase for Garcia’s improvisational fire, with Phil Lesh locking in tight bass lines and Bob Weir adding shining moments throughout the jam. The band then rolls straight into Saint Stephen and Mason’s Children without missing a beat, creating a seamless flow that many reviewers call a “powerful set.” After the centerpiece, the group drives through Good Lovin’, Uncle John’s Band, and a double Turn On Your Lovelight medley that keeps the energy high to the very end. While a few recordings note an audible edit on Mason’s Children or occasional tape artifacts, the overall performance is consistently praised for its intensity and cohesion, making this show a standout entry in the early‑70 catalog.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: Strong positive sentiment across multiple recordings: descriptors like “epic Dark Star,” “smoking solo,” “transcendent,” and consistent praise for the St. Stephen → Mason’s Children flow indicate a highly regarded performance. No recurring negative comments about musical execution were found, only mixed remarks about audio quality.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with crystal‑clear fidelity; preserves the epic Dark Star and overall set flow despite a brief edit on Mason’s Children.

key_highlights: Marathon Dark Star that showcases Garcia’s transcendent soloing.
Seamless Saint Stephen → Mason’s Children transition keeps momentum high.
Tight interplay between Jerry and Phil during the extended jam.
Energetic second half featuring Good Lovin’, Uncle John’s Band and a double Turn On Your Lovelight.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers a smoking, transcendent solo on Dark Star and drives the improvisational fire throughout the set.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides tight, supportive bass work that interlocks perfectly with Garcia during the marathon jam.
band_performance.Bob: Weir contributes notable moments within the extended Dark Star and adds solid rhythm throughout.
band_performance.Pigpen: A Pigpen tribute is noted in the liner notes for Turn On Your Lovelight; otherwise his presence is low‑key on this show.
